title: Mechanical Engineer
text:
About Chemify
Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world’s largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.
Our Chemifarm facility in Glasgow operates a growing fleet of advanced robotic systems that automate synthesis, optimisation, and library generation. This gives our computational scientists something rare: a direct, high-throughput bridge from in silico design to physically synthesised molecules, closing the design–make–test loop at a pace conventional drug discovery organisations cannot match.
Location: Glasgow, UK (on-site)
Travel: Minimal
The Role
We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer to design and develop the mechanical systems that make up our robotic synthesis platform — the fluidic handling, motion assemblies, enclosures, and instrument modules that physically carry out chemistry. You will take designs from concept through detailed CAD, prototyping, and testing into production, working closely with electronics, firmware, and manufacturing engineers.
What sets this role apart is that your designs do not just move — they handle real reagents and run real chemistry, so precision, reliability, and material compatibility matter as much as elegant mechanics.
If designing mechanical systems for a real-world robotic platform sounds like the right shape of job for you, we’d love to welcome you to our team.
Key Responsibilities
- Design mechanical assemblies and components — motion systems, fluidics, fixtures, and enclosures — from concept to production.
- Produce detailed 3D CAD models, drawings, and tolerance analyses.
- Prototype, test, and iterate hardware, validating designs against real-world performance.
- Partner with electronics and firmware engineers on integrated electromechanical modules.
- Work with manufacturing and supply chain on design-for-manufacture, materials, and component selection.
- Contribute to design reviews and the team’s mechanical standards. About You
You are a hands-on mechanical engineer who enjoys taking a design from sketch to working hardware. You sweat the details — tolerances, materials, manufacturability — and you like seeing your parts come together and move in the real world.
We expect you to bring:
- Proven experience in mechanical design engineering, ideally for precision electromechanical or robotic hardware.
- Strong CAD skills (e.g. SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or similar) and detailed drawing / GD&T experience.
- Sound grasp of mechanisms, materials, tolerancing, and design-for-manufacture.
- Hands-on prototyping and testing experience.
- Close collaboration with electronics, firmware, and manufacturing engineers. Beneficial Skills
- Experience with fluidics, pumps, valves, or motion systems.
- Exposure to lab instrumentation, robotics, or automation hardware.
- Familiarity with manufacturing processes (machining, sheet metal, injection moulding, 3D printing).
- FEA or tolerance-stack analysis.
Why Join Chemify?
Impact.   The mechanical systems you design are the body of our platform — your work is what physically carries out chemistry in the Chemifarm.
Autonomy.   You will own mechanical design across modules and shape how our hardware is built.
Ambition.   We are a Series B deep-tech company at the frontier of chemistry, robotics, and AI — with the resources and mandate to design mechanical systems for a platform unlike anything else.

title: Senior Software Engineer
text:
Location: Glasgow • Workstyle: Hybrid • Reports to : VP Software Engineering
We're open on level for the right person, this role can be scoped at Staff for a candidate with deeper platform ownership experience.
About Chemify
Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world's largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.
The Role
Everything Chemify does runs on the Unified Data Platform. When a molecule is designed, registered, sourced, synthesised by a robot, tested, and shipped, the platform is what carries it, one canonical identity for every chemical entity, one trusted answer for its properties and hazards, one record of what was actually made and shipped to clients.
We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to own crucial parts of that platform. This is a genuinely full-stack role: you'll own applications end-to-end, the interfaces chemists and operations staff use every day, the services behind them, and the data pipelines that feed them.
The platform spans seven domains, chemical identity and registration, chemical safety, inventory, sourcing, reaction data, reference data, and the shared infrastructure underneath. You won't work across all of it, but you won't be boxed into one corner either. We'll match your area to your strengths and appetite, and we expect that to change as the platform grows. What stays constant is the level of ownership: your systems, your architecture calls, your users.
You'll work in a tight-knit, cross-functional environment spanning software, chemistry, operations, and programme management, the kind of place where curiosity across disciplines is an asset, not a distraction.
If you enjoy solving complex technical problems that make a real-world impact, are a natural communicator, and are energised by working closely with scientists using cutting-edge technology, we'd love to hear from you.
What You'll Work On
Applications people rely on daily. Full ownership of user-facing systems used by chemists, analysts, and operations teams across multiple sites, from the interface through to the data model.
Services that are the single source of truth. Registration and reference services where being authoritative matters, and where every other system is a consumer with its own expectations.
Domain modelling that has to be right. Chemical entities, batches, lineage, properties, hazards. These are hard models with real edge cases, and the abstractions you choose will outlive the code.
Data pipelines and orchestration. Dagster pipelines feeding a versioned data lake and a warehouse serving multiple use cases, with the reproducibility and governance that scientific data demands.
Reconciling sources that disagree. External datasets, vendor systems, and instruments that each claim a different truth, promoting trusted values into the systems everyone else depends on.
Key Responsibilities
- Own the full lifecycle of the applications and services in your area: scoping, architecture, development, deployment, and monitoring production.
- Design data models and workflows covering a wide range of use cases across AI chemistry, synthesis, and manufacturing.
- Build and maintain robust, observable pipelines for internal, client-specific, and literature data.
- Work directly with chemists and operations staff to understand how the work actually happens, not how the spec says it happens.
- Collaborate with Infrastructure to ensure new work is soundly architected and production-ready.
- Define and champion engineering and data best practices: versioning, testing, documentation, governance, data contracts.
- Mentor engineers and contribute to communities of practice across the team.
- Contribute to team-wide initiatives: code reviews, design discussions, ADRs, process improvements, and workstream planning.
What You'll Bring
Core
- Significant commercial software engineering experience.
- Strong Python, with production experience in FastAPI, Django, Flask, or similar.
- PostgreSQL fluency, schema design, query optimisation, and ORM frameworks such as SQLAlchemy/SQLModel.
- Commercial experience with TypeScript and React, and a genuine interest in UI/UX.
- Experience building and maintaining data-intensive applications, you're comfortable on both sides of the application/data boundary.
- Comfortable with containerised deployments (Docker) and CI/CD pipelines (GitLab, ArgoCD).
- Hands-on with AWS or another major cloud platform.
- Experience integrating with systems you don't own, negotiating contracts, handling partial failure, and enabling teams to own their data.
- You've genuinely rewired how you work around AI-assisted development tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or equivalent), this is part of how we work, not a nice-to-have.
- Strong communicator, genuinely collaborative, comfortable with non-technical domain experts as your primary users.
Infrastructure & Data
- Working knowledge of Kubernetes/EKS, comfortable deploying to and reasoning about containerised workloads in a managed K8s environment.
- Experience orchestrating pipelines with Dagster, Airflow, Prefect, or similar.
- Solid grasp of ETL concepts and production-grade pipeline design.
​ Beneficial Skills
- Interest in chemistry, life sciences, robotics, or manufacturing.
- Hands-on experience with scientific data, chemical, biological, or laboratory.
- Experience building systems where the data model represents physical things, and being out of sync with reality has consequences.
- Previous experience in AI drug discovery is a genuine differentiator for us.
- Interest in semantic technologies (graph databases, ontologies) or modern data stack.
- Experience enabling analytics teams by building data models for BI tools and dashboards.
- Familiarity with Infrastructure as Code (AWS CDK or Terraform) is a strong plus.
- Experience with product design thinking and tools such as Figma.
- A degree in Computer Science, a scientific discipline, or a related field, useful, not required. We care what you've built.
Why Join Chemify?
Impact: You'll own foundational parts of the platform that every other team at Chemify builds on, accelerating discovery and unlocking new possibilities in science and medicine.
Ownership: Real architectural authority over systems that matter, not tickets from someone else's backlog.
Autonomy: Reporting to the VP Software Engineering, you'll have genuine influence over technical direction and product quality.
Ambition: Series B, scaling rapidly, tackling problems at the frontier of robotics, AI, and chemistry. We're building the right foundations for the future.

title: Senior Firmware Engineer
text:
About Chemify
Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world’s largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.
Location: Glasgow, UK (hybrid)
The Role
We are seeking a Senior Firmware Engineer to own the embedded firmware that drives the robotic modules at the heart of our platform — the pumps, valves, sensors, and motion systems that physically carry out chemistry. You will take firmware from architecture through to robust, production-grade code running across our fleet of robotic systems, working closely with electronics, mechanical, and platform-software engineers.
What sets this role apart is how close to the chemistry you will be: the firmware you write is the layer where code becomes physical motion and real reactions — and as a senior engineer you will shape how that layer is built.
If owning embedded firmware on a platform that makes molecules sounds like the right shape of job for you, we’d love to welcome you to our team.
Key Responsibilities
• Architect, develop, test, and maintain embedded firmware for instrument and robotics modules.
• Own firmware for subsystems end to end — from requirements and design through bring-up, validation, and production.
• Work close to the metal: microcontrollers, motion control, sensors, actuators, and communication buses.
• Partner with electronics engineers on board bring-up and hardware/firmware interfaces, and with platform-software on higher-level control.
• Drive firmware quality: testing, code review, CI for embedded, and robust real-time behaviour.
• Mentor junior firmware engineers and help set the team’s embedded standards and practices.
About You
You are an experienced embedded engineer who likes owning firmware from architecture to hardware on the bench. You care about robustness in the real world — where a missed edge case means a stalled robot, not just a failed test — and you raise the bar for the people around you.
We expect you to bring:
• 5+ years developing embedded/firmware for electromechanical or robotic systems, including production-grade work.
• Strong C/C++ (and ideally [Python] for tooling/test), with solid embedded fundamentals.
• Deep understanding of microcontrollers, real-time behaviour, interrupts, timers, and communication buses (I²C, SPI, UART, CAN).
• Hands-on bring-up and debugging across the firmware/hardware boundary (oscilloscope, logic analyser), with a methodical approach to root cause.
• STM32 experience.
• Experience owning firmware subsystems end to end and lifting the people around you.
Beneficial Skills
• Motion control, closed-loop control, or RTOS experience.
• Familiarity with hardware design and reading schematics, and close collaboration with electronics engineers.
• Exposure to robotics, lab instrumentation, or other precision electromechanical systems.
• Embedded CI/test infrastructure and firmware-update/bootloader design.
Why Join Chemify?
Impact. Your firmware is where digital instructions become physical chemistry — the robotic modules you bring to life run real experiments in the Chemifarm.
Autonomy. You will own firmware subsystems across the platform and shape how we build embedded software.
Ambition. We are a Series B deep-tech company at the frontier of chemistry, robotics, and AI — with the resources and mandate to build embedded systems for a platform unlike anything else.

title: Automation Scientist
text:
About Chemify
Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world’s largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.
Our Chemifarm facility in Glasgow operates a growing fleet of advanced robotic systems that automate synthesis, optimisation, and library generation. This gives our computational scientists something rare: a direct, high-throughput bridge from in silico design to physically synthesised molecules, closing the design–make–test loop at a pace conventional drug discovery organisations cannot match.
Location: Glasgow, UK (on-site)
Travel: Minimal
The Role
We are seeking an Automation Scientist to sit at the intersection of chemistry, engineering, and testing — translating real chemistry onto our robotic synthesis platform and making sure it works. You will take synthetic routes and turn them into automated protocols, run and validate them on our robotic systems, diagnose issues that span chemistry, hardware, firmware, and software, and feed what you learn back to the engineering teams building the platform.
What sets this role apart is the hybrid: you will need a chemist’s judgement, an engineer’s instinct for how the machines work, and a tester’s rigour — all on a platform where code becomes molecules.
If working across chemistry, engineering, and testing on a real-world robotic platform sounds like the right shape of job for you, we’d love to welcome you to our team.
Key Responsibilities
- Translate synthetic chemistry into automated protocols that run on our robotic platform.
- Run, validate, and troubleshoot syntheses end to end, diagnosing issues across chemistry, hardware, firmware, and software.
- Act as the bridge between the chemistry and engineering teams, turning lab reality into clear, actionable feedback.
- Define and run test protocols and acceptance criteria that prove the platform performs against real chemistry.
- Help characterise and improve platform capability, reliability, and reproducibility.
- Contribute to protocols, documentation, and the standards that make automated chemistry repeatable. About You
You are a scientist who likes machines — as comfortable reasoning about a reaction as about the robot running it. You enjoy being the person who works out why something did not behave, whether the cause is chemistry, hardware, or code, and you communicate clearly across disciplines.
We expect you to bring:
- A degree in chemistry or a related science (PhD or equivalent hands-on experience welcome), with real synthetic / wet-lab experience.
- A strong practical bent and genuine interest in automation, robotics, and how the underlying systems work.
- Experience running, validating, and troubleshooting experiments rigorously and reproducibly.
- The ability to work across chemistry, engineering, and software teams and translate between them.
- Careful, methodical working and clear record-keeping. Beneficial Skills
- Experience with automated or high-throughput synthesis / lab systems.
- Familiarity with analytical techniques (e.g. HPLC, LC-MS, NMR) for validating outcomes.
- Some scripting ([Python]) for protocols, data handling, or analysis.
- Exposure to flow chemistry, process chemistry, or lab-automation hardware.
- An understanding of how software and hardware combine to run an experiment.
Why Join Chemify?
Impact.   You are where chemistry meets the machine — your work is what turns our platform’s capability into real, reproducible synthesis.
Autonomy.   You will own the translation of chemistry onto the platform and the testing that proves it works, with real influence over how we make automated chemistry reliable.
Ambition.   We are a Series B deep-tech company at the frontier of chemistry, robotics, and AI — a chance to work across chemistry, engineering, and automation on systems no one else has.

title: Health and Safety Advisor
text:
About Chemify
Chemify is transforming how molecules are designed, manufactured and discovered through a combination of chemistry, automation and artificial intelligence. Operating at the forefront of chemical innovation, we provide a dynamic environment where safety, quality and operational excellence are fundamental to our success.
As our operations continue to grow, we are seeking a motivated and ambitious Health & Safety Advisor who is looking to develop their career. This role provides a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience across laboratory, manufacturing, engineering and operational environments while contributing to the continuous development of our health, safety and compliance systems.
The Opportunity
This role is ideally suited to an individual who has a solid foundation in health and safety and is ready to take the next step in their career.
Working closely with the Health & Safety Manager and operational leadership teams, you will gain exposure to:
- Health and Safety management systems.
- ISO 9001 implementation and auditing.
- ISO 45001 preparation.
- Regulatory compliance and inspections.
- Incident investigation and Root Cause Analysis (RCA).
- Safety leadership and culture development.
- Strategic health and safety planning.
As the business continues to grow, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to take ownership of larger projects and progressively develop into a future Health & Safety Manager role.
Key Responsibilities
Compliance & Governance
- Support compliance with UK health and safety legislation and associated regulations.
- Assist in maintaining ISO 45001 and ISO 9001 management systems.
- Participate in internal audits, inspections and compliance reviews.
- Support regulatory inspections and customer audits.
Risk Management
- Assist with risk assessments, COSHH assessments and DSEAR assessments.
- Support permit-to-work activities and contractor management.
- Participate in incident investigations and Root Cause Analysis.
- Track corrective and preventative actions through to completion.
Training & Communication
- Deliver health and safety inductions and awareness training.
- Support development of toolbox talks, safety campaigns and communications.
- Promote employee engagement in health and safety initiatives.
Monitoring & Reporting
- Conduct workplace inspections and behavioural observations.
- Monitor accident, near miss and hazard reporting systems.
- Support KPI reporting and trend analysis.
- Assist with emergency preparedness exercises and response planning.
Continuous Improvement
- Identify opportunities to improve safety performance and compliance.
- Support implementation of safety improvement projects.
- Contribute to the ongoing development of company policies, procedures and standards.
- Gradually assume ownership of selected management system elements as experience develops.
Skills & Experience
Essential
- NEBOSH General Certificate (or equivalent).
- Experience in a laboratory, manufacturing, engineering or industrial environment.
- Excellent understanding of UK health and safety legislation.
- Experience supporting risk assessments and incident investigations.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
Desirable
- Working towards NEBOSH Diploma or equivalent qualification.
- Experience with ISO 45001 management systems.
- Knowledge of COSHH, DSEAR, PUWER and LOLER.
- Internal auditing experience.
- IOSH membership.
What We're Looking For
We are looking for someone who:
- Has genuine enthusiasm for health and safety.
- Wants to build a long-term career in safety leadership.
- Is proactive, inquisitive and eager to learn.
- Can positively influence and engage colleagues at all levels.
- Is comfortable balancing operational support with strategic improvement activities.
- Is motivated by the opportunity to progress into a future Health & Safety Manager position.
What We Offer
- A clear development pathway towards a Health & Safety Manager role.
- Exposure to a diverse range of laboratory, engineering and manufacturing activities.
- Support towards further professional qualifications and development.
- Opportunities to lead improvement projects and influence company-wide safety initiatives.
- The chance to help shape the future safety culture of a rapidly growing technology and chemical manufacturing business.

title: Project Manager
text:
About Chemify
Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world’s largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.

We are seeking an experienced Project Manager to join Chemify at a critical stage of growth. This is a high-impact role working closely with the Executive Leadership Team to translate strategic priorities into well-defined, executable projects across the company.
You will own and deliver a portfolio of company-wide and operationally focused initiatives, many of which originate directly from the executive board. These projects will span operational efficiency, platform development, cross-functional process improvement, and scaling the business.
You’ll operate as the central orchestration point for complex, multi-disciplinary delivery across software, hardware, operations, and chemistry teams. While this role does not require scientific or chemistry expertise, it does require a highly capable Project Manager who is comfortable working at executive level, driving clarity, accountability, and momentum in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.
If you thrive on bringing structure to complexity, enjoy working across diverse teams, and are motivated by helping ambitious organisations execute strategy at scale, we’d love to hear from you.

- Own and deliver a portfolio of executive-sponsored projects, translating strategic objectives into clear scopes, plans, milestones, and outcomes.
- Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives spanning Operations, Platform (Software & Hardware), Engineering, and Process.
- Act as the primary coordination point between executives, project teams, and delivery owners, ensuring alignment and accountability.

- Partner closely with Software and Hardware teams to enable platform development, coordinating roadmaps, timelines, and dependencies.
- Establish and maintain appropriate project governance, delivery cadence, and reporting structures.
- Identify, manage, and mitigate risks, dependencies, and bottlenecks that could impact delivery.

What you’ll bring

- Comfort operating in high-growth, startup or scale-up environments with ambiguity and pace.

- Experience establishing or operating within a PMO environment.
- Strong understanding of delivery governance, prioritisation, and dependency management.
- Experience driving operational efficiency or transformation projects .
- Familiarity with Agile, hybrid, or waterfall delivery models.
- Data-driven approach, using metrics to inform decisions and measure impact.
- Experience working in deep-tech, platform, or highly technical organisations.
​
Why Join Chemify?
Impact:
You will play a central role in delivering projects that directly influence our growth, customer experience, and operational success. Your work won’t sit in a project plan — it will drive tangible outcomes across the business.
Ownership:
You’ll have the autonomy to lead projects from initiation through to delivery, working closely with senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams. We trust our Project Managers to make decisions, solve problems, and create momentum.
Opportunity:
As a growing business, there is significant scope to shape how we work, improve processes, and contribute beyond the boundaries of a traditional project management role. You’ll be joining at a stage where your ideas and leadership can have a lasting impact.

title: CADD Scientist / Senior CADD Scientist
text:
Location : Glasgow
About Chemify:
Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world's largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.
Our Chemifarm facility in Glasgow operates a growing fleet of advanced robotic systems that automate synthesis, optimisation, and library generation. This gives our computational scientists something rare: a direct, high-throughput bridge from in silico design to physically synthesised molecules, closing the design–make–test loop at a pace conventional drug discovery organisations cannot match.
The Role
We are seeking a CADD Scientist to drive computer-aided drug design on Chemify's commercial programmes and computational platform. You will sit within a cross-disciplinary team — computational chemists, in-house and partner medicinal chemists, AI researchers, data engineers, and automation scientists — and help translate structure, simulation, and machine learning into molecules we actually make.
What sets this role apart is the design–make–test loop: working directly with partner chemists on medicinal-chemistry strategy, you will design and prioritise molecules for synthesis and see them physically made on our robotic platform within days rather than months.
If you are energised by solving complex problems at the intersection of chemistry, physics, and AI — and by seeing your designs synthesised and tested in days — we'd love to welcome you to our team.
Key Responsibilities
- Run computational design across the CADD stack — docking, pharmacophore, shape and 3D-similarity, MD, FEP, and QSAR — choosing appropriate physics- and ML-based approaches for each question.
- Design, enumerate, and prioritise molecules and libraries for synthesis, and triage and analyse the results across DMTL cycles.
- Work with in-house and partner chemists on MPO, translating SAR and diverse assay readouts into actionable, biologically relevant design hypotheses.
- Communicate computational reasoning, trade-offs, and recommendations clearly to working chemists and project leads.
- Apply modern deep learning for molecular design (GNNs, generative models, property prediction) where it complements traditional CADD methods.
- Contribute to productionising CADD methods into a reproducible, API-first toolkit; partner with Infrastructure on cost-effective GPU/HPC workflows.
- Own the computational design strategy on assigned programmes from hit discovery through lead optimisation; mentor junior CADD scientists, partner with the Head of Advanced Machine Learning on growth, and act as the scientific interface with customers.
About You
You are a credible computational chemist who is equally comfortable reasoning about protein–ligand interactions and shipping code that runs in production. You care about getting real molecules made, not only writing elegant methods.
We expect you to bring:
- PhD (or equivalent experience) in Computational Chemistry, Structural Biology, Biophysics, Physics, or a closely related field — with 2+ years (CADD Scientist) or 5+ years (Senior) of hands-on CADD experience in small-molecule drug discovery.
- Grounding in both structure- and ligand-based drug design — protein–ligand biophysics on one side, and pharmacophore, shape, and SAR-driven design on the other — with hands-on use of the standard CADD stack (e.g. MOE, PyMOL, OpenMM / GROMACS / AMBER).
- Familiarity with core drug discovery and medicinal chemistry principles, and the ability to translate diverse assay readouts into biologically relevant design hypotheses.
- Strong Python and at least one core cheminformatics toolkit (e.g. RDKit, OpenEye); real experience inside the drug-discovery loop (SAR, MPO, DMTL cycles, library enumeration); comfort with GPU-accelerated simulation and cloud/HPC workflows.
- Working knowledge of modern deep learning for molecular design (GNNs, generative models, property prediction), and a clear sense of when these complement traditional CADD methods rather than replace them.
- (Senior level) A track record of owning the computational strategy on active programmes, and of technical leadership — mentoring and influencing scientific direction beyond your own projects.
Beneficial Skills
- Hands-on experience with free energy perturbation (FEP+, OpenFE, or equivalent) in a production drug-discovery setting.
- Practical use of generative chemistry methods (diffusion, autoregressive, RL-based design), including a clear-eyed view of their failure modes.
- Familiarity with active learning, iterative DMTL design loops, and Bayesian optimisation applied to molecular design.
- Experience building or integrating CADD tooling into API-first platforms (FastAPI, Docker, CI/CD), and proficiency in C/C++ / CUDA for high-performance computational chemistry.
- A visible track record in the field — peer-reviewed publications, open-source contributions, or public projects that demonstrate your judgement on real CADD problems.
Why Join Chemify?
Impact:
​ You will directly shape the molecules Chemify designs and makes — at a company uniquely positioned to close the design–make–test loop through automated chemical synthesis at scale.
Autonomy:
Reporting to the Head of Advanced Machine Learning, you will shape the computational platform behind every project at Chemify.
Ambition:
We are a Series B deep-tech company investing in world-class infrastructure and tackling problems at the frontier of AI, robotics, and chemistry. You will have the resources, the data, and the mandate to do CADD in a way that isn't possible elsewhere.

title: Analytical Technician
text:
About Chemify
Chemify is creating a future where important molecules, drugs and currently unimaginable new materials are instantly accessible; thereby radically increasing the speed of innovation, quality of life, and reach of humanity. The company is building the infrastructure to digitize chemistry for the design, discovery and synthesis of new molecules with the desired function and properties instantly and on-demand. Chemify has built a platform that combines purpose-built programming languages, robotics, AI, and the world’s largest and continuously growing database of chemical programs to accelerate chemical discovery to new, transformative heights.
Chemify is supported by some of the best investors from Silicon Valley and across the world, including Triatomic Capital, BlueYard ventures, DCVC, Founders Fund, and others.
Job Purpose
As an Analytical Technician (all levels) , you will provide the organization with expert insights and know-how for the analytical data acquisition with NMR and UPLC-MS. Ideally you bring knowledge and experience of sample preparation and running of UPLC-MS/LCMS and/or NMR systems. You will help develop the world’s most advanced automated chemical manufacturing lab, collaborating with software and engineering teams to troubleshoot and improve our proprietary technology. We value a flat structure where every member takes ownership and influences our scientific direction.
Shift Pattern
This role will involve working one of several shifts (e.g. early, late, nightshift, weekend).
Location
This role will be based at one of our sites in Glasgow.
Who we are looking for
The ideal candidate will be a smart, enthusiastic, energetic and ambitious individual excited to wear many hats and contribute to the overall success of the company as the needs evolve. ​
We welcome applications from candidates with HNC/HND qualifications in Applied Sciences/Chemistry or relevant degrees who can demonstrate significant hands-on laboratory experience and a desire to work in a high-throughput manufacturing environment.
Key Responsibilities
- Sample Management: Prepare and submit analytical samples for UPLC and NMR and run and analyse TLC samples.
- System Upkeep: Prepare mobile phases/buffers and perform routine maintenance on UPLC and NMR systems.
- Troubleshooting: Diagnose instrument issues internally or via vendors.
- Collaboration: Work with chemists and lab ops to maximize workflow effectiveness.
- Innovation: Partner with engineering and software teams to test automation updates and suggest platform improvements.
- Process Development: Proactively design more efficient analysis workflows.
- Documentation: Record experiments accurately and adapt to changing company priorities.
Qualifications and Experience
- Minimum Higher (or equivalent) in English, mathematics and a science subject. HNC/HND or degree in in a scientific field with laboratory experience.
- The candidate should have previous work or study experience in a technical role within a laboratory environment, including the handling of chemicals
- Good numeracy, literacy and attention to detail
- Ability to follow defined procedures accurately
- Oral and written communication skills (English fluency)
Number of Positions
We are looking to fill two positions with start dates between February and April 2026.
UK Right to Work
Please note that the company are unable to sponsor visas for this role.

title: Junior Full Stack Engineer

About Chemify
Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world’s largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.
Location: San Francisco, US (hybrid)
The Role
We are seeking a Junior Full Stack Software Engineer to join the team building the software behind Chemify’s robotic synthesis platform. You will work across the stack on real features — from backend services to the interfaces scientists use — with senior engineers close at hand to review your work and help you grow fast.
What sets this role apart is the platform itself: a rare early-career seat where the software you write helps physically make molecules, not just move data around.
If learning fast across the full stack on a real-world platform sounds like the right shape of job for you, we’d love to welcome you to our team.
Key Responsibilities
• Build and ship full-stack features under the guidance of senior engineers.
• Fix bugs, write tests, and improve tooling across backend services and web front-ends.
• Learn how the platform turns experiment definitions into robotic execution, and contribute to it.
• Take part in code reviews, design discussions — growing your ownership over time.
About You
You are early in your career but serious about the craft — curious, quick to learn, and energised by hard problems. You ask good questions, act on feedback, and want to grow alongside engineers who will push you.
We expect you to bring:
• 0–2 years of software experience (internships, projects, or a strong portfolio count).
• Working knowledge of at least one backend language ([Python/C/C++)
• Strong fundamentals and a genuine appetite to learn quickly.
• Clear communication and comfort asking questions and acting on feedback.
Beneficial Skills
• A degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field — or equivalent self-taught proof.
• Any exposure to robotics, hardware, lab automation, or scientific computing.
Why Join Chemify?
Impact. Even early on, your work ships into a platform that physically makes molecules — you will see the results of what you build.
Autonomy. You will be trusted with real features from the start and given room to grow your ownership.
Ambition. We are a Series B deep-tech company at the frontier of AI, robotics, and chemistry — a place to learn fast, surrounded by people who will raise your bar.

title: Production Chemist
text:
About Chemify
Chemify is creating a future where important molecules, drugs and currently unimaginable new materials are instantly accessible; thereby radically increasing the speed of innovation, quality of life, and reach of humanity. The company is building the infrastructure to digitize chemistry for the design, discovery and synthesis of new molecules with the desired function and properties instantly and on-demand. Chemify has built a platform that combines purpose-built programming languages, robotics, AI, and the world’s largest and continuously growing database of chemical programs to accelerate chemical discovery to new, transformative heights.
Chemify is supported by some of the best investors from Silicon Valley and across the world, including Triatomic Capital, BlueYard ventures, DCVC, Founders Fund, and others.
Job Purpose
The Production Chemist will support the production team in efficiently executing critical manufacturing tasks to ensure high-quality, high-throughput and safe chemical manufacturing. While working within the laboratory the Production Chemist must be observant of safety standards and operating procedures.
Who we are looking for
The ideal candidate will be a smart, enthusiastic, energetic and ambitious individual excited to wear many hats and contribute to the overall success of the company as the needs evolve.​
We welcome applications from candidates with HNC/HND qualifications in Applied Sciences/Chemistry or relevant degrees who can demonstrate significant hands-on laboratory experience and a desire to work in a high-throughput manufacturing environment.
Key Responsibilities
- Be a key member of the Production Team
- Setup of automated chemical reactions using our proprietary Curie, Lovelace and Arnold platforms
- Carry out automated and manual chemistry operations (e.g. filtrations, workups and evaporations)
- Maintaining laboratory housekeeping
- Take on growing responsibilities during the transformation of the company from an R&D stage organisation to an operational powerhouse
- Taking the initiative to suggest improvements to working practices
- Accurate and timely documentation of completed tasks using our own digital laboratory notebook
Qualifications and Experience
- Minimum Higher (or equivalent) in English, mathematics and a science subject. HNC/HND or degree in relevant field preferred.
- The candidate should have previous work or study experience in a technical role within a laboratory environment, including the handling of chemicals
- Good numeracy, literacy and attention to detail
- Ability to follow defined procedures accurately
- Oral and written communication skills (English fluency)
Location
This role will be based at the company’s new manufacturing site at OakBank Industrial Estate, Garscube Road, Glasgow, G20 7LU.
Shift Pattern
This role will involve working one of several shifts (e.g. early, late, nightshift, weekend).
Number of Positions
We are looking to fill 5 positions with start dates between February and April 2026.
UK Right to Work
Please note that the company are unable to sponsor visas for this role.

title: Senior / Staff Machine Learning Scientist
text:
About Chemify:
Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world's largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.
Our Chemifarm facility in Glasgow operates a growing fleet of advanced robotic systems that automate synthesis, optimisation, and library generation. This gives our computational scientists something rare: a direct, high-throughput bridge from in silico design to physically synthesised molecules, closing the design–make–test loop at a pace conventional drug discovery organisations cannot match.
Location:  Glasgow (onsite, full-time) or fully remote with regular travel to our Glasgow HQ / Chemifarm
The Role
We are seeking a Senior / Staff Machine Learning Scientist to work across the breadth of Chemify's platform — generative models for chemistry, search and planning for retrosynthesis, computer vision for telemetry from our robotic systems, and agentic workflows that tie it all together. You will partner with computational chemists, CADD scientists, software engineers, and hardware engineers, and apply AI/ML to build the next generation of Chemify's platform.
What sets this role apart is the combination of breadth of ML problems — generative chemistry, vision, search, agents — paired with a robotic platform that turns your models into physical experiments.
If working across a wide range of hard ML problems on a real-world platform sounds like the right shape of job for you, we'd love to welcome you to our team.
Key Responsibilities
- Build generative and foundation chemistry models for molecular design.
- Advance retrosynthesis and synthesis-aware ML by leveraging Chemify's reaction database and robot-execution data.
- Apply computer vision to transform robot telemetry into models that monitor process state and feedback into experimental control.
- Prototype agentic workflows that orchestrate models, tools, and the platform — closing loops between proposal, execution, observation, and learning.
- Productionise models into a reproducible, API-first toolkit; partner with Infrastructure on GPU training and HPC; maintain high standards of ML best practices, including rigorous evaluation, benchmarks, and reproducibility.
- Mentor junior ML scientists, partner with the Head of Advanced Machine Learning on hiring and growth, and represent Chemify's AI/ML capability externally.
- (Staff level)  Set technical direction across the AI/ML stack; lead cross-cutting initiatives spanning chemistry models, retrosynthesis, vision, and agents.
​
About You
You are an experienced ML scientist who is equally comfortable training models and shipping the code that other people end up building on. You care about whether your model changes a real decision — not just whether it beats a benchmark. You're at home moving across problem types, from generative models to vision to search.
​
We expect you to bring:
- PhD or equivalent experience in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Statistics, Physics, or a related quantitative field — 5+ years (Senior) or 8+ years (Staff) of hands-on applied ML experience, including production-grade work.
- Deep familiarity with modern deep learning stack (PyTorch or JAX), and breadth across at least two of: generative models (diffusion, autoregressive, flow-based), graph and equivariant networks, vision (CNNs, ViTs, multimodal LLMs), search and planning (MCTS, A*), or agentic / RL systems.
- Experience taking ML from prototype to production: reproducible pipelines, distributed jobs, and batch workflows on cloud (AWS / GCP / Azure) or HPC.
- Strong scientific computing instincts: clean Python, careful experiment design, leakage-aware splits, and rigorous benchmarks.
- Clear communication with non-ML scientists and engineers and a willingness to pick up new domains (you don't need to know chemistry on day one).
- (Staff level)  A track record of technical leadership: mentoring, setting standards, and influencing scientific and technical direction beyond your own projects.
​
Beneficial Skills
- Practical experience with active learning, Bayesian optimisation, conformal prediction, or uncertainty quantification in iterative real-world loops.
- Familiarity with retrosynthesis ML, computer-aided synthesis planning (CASP), or reaction-condition / yield prediction.
- Working knowledge of how ML fits into a drug-discovery or materials-design workflow, plus familiarity with cheminformatics tooling (e.g. RDKit, OpenEye) — or willingness to pick these up.
- MLOps fluency: experiment tracking, data versioning, model serving, and observability of deployed models.
- A visible track record in the field — peer-reviewed publications, open-source contributions, or public projects that demonstrate your judgement on real ML problems.
​
Why Join Chemify?
Impact:
Your models will directly shape what Chemify's robotic platform proposes, plans, and observes — at a company uniquely positioned to close the loop between design and physical experiment.
Autonomy:
Reporting to the Head of Advanced Machine Learning, you will work across the AI/ML problems with the most impact, and have meaningful influence over the direction of our AI/ML capability.
Ambition:
We are a Series B deep-tech company investing in world-class infrastructure and tackling problems at the frontier of AI, robotics, and chemistry. You will have the resources and the mandate to do AI/ML in a way that isn't possible elsewhere — across chemistry, vision, search, and autonomous systems on the same platform.
This vacancy has now been closed. Thank you for your interest.

Chemify is revolutionising chemistry. We are creating a future where the synthesis of previously unimaginable molecules, drugs, and materials is instantly accessible. By combining AI, robotics, and the world’s largest continually expanding database of chemical programs, we are accelerating chemical discovery to improve quality of life and extend the reach of humanity.

We are seeking a Senior Full Stack Software Engineer to build the software that turns Chemify’s robotic synthesis platform into something scientists can drive — the services that schedule and execute runs across racks of robotic hardware, and the interfaces chemists use to design, launch, and monitor experiments. You will partner with firmware, hardware, manufacturing, and chemistry teams, and own meaningful slices of the platform end to end.
What sets this role apart is that the “stack” reaches all the way down to real instruments: the code you ship has physical consequences in the lab, and you can watch your work turn digital intent into synthesised molecules.

title: Senior Product Owner
text:
About Chemify
Chemify is pioneering “Chemputation”, a digital chemistry platform that combines software, artificial intelligence and robotics to automate the design, synthesis and discovery of new molecules. Spun out of research led by Professor Lee Cronin and headquartered in Glasgow, Chemify is scaling its platform to accelerate chemical discovery for partners across pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and materials science.
As the company grows, software is central to how Chemify's chemistry, robotics and AI capabilities come together, and this role will help shape it.
The Role
Chemify is looking for an experienced Senior Product Owner to join our Operations & Fulfilment team and lead product for our Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and its peripheral applications. This is the software our scientists and operations teams rely on to plan, run and track production and fulfilment work. You'll work at the intersection of software engineering, chemistry and operations, turning the needs of our internal users into a clear, prioritised roadmap and backlog that you and the engineering team shape and deliver together.
This role combines product direction with hands-on product ownership, and is built on partnership with engineering. You'll shape where the MES is heading together with the engineering team lead, bringing the user and operational perspective while drawing on the team's technical insight to decide what we build and when. You'll also own the day-to-day backlog that gets us there. Day to day you'll also work closely with our scientists and operations team, so it suits someone who enjoys solving novel problems alongside the people who use the software.
Key Responsibilities
• Own and prioritise the product backlog for the MES and its peripheral applications, working with the engineering team lead to balance operational, scientific and technical priorities.
• Shape the product direction for the MES in partnership with the engineering team lead, working with users and stakeholders to understand operational needs and translating them into a clear, well-sequenced roadmap, epics, user stories and acceptance criteria.
• Act as the primary link between the engineering team and stakeholders across chemistry, operations and leadership, communicating priorities, timelines and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Facilitate backlog refinement and story prioritisation with the engineering team within an Agile/Scrum framework, and bring the user perspective to sprint planning and reviews.
• Define, track and report on product success metrics and KPIs, using data to inform prioritisation decisions.
• Work with the engineering team, and with UX, data and platform teams where needed, to ensure the software is intuitive for scientists and operators and robust enough for automated, high-throughput use.
• Identify risks, dependencies and blockers early, including those involving other teams, and work through them together with the engineering team lead.
• Stay close to end users, the scientists and operations teams who rely on the MES day to day, so that the product makes a real difference to how their work gets done.
What We're Looking For
• Proven years' of experience as a Product Owner or Product Manager in a software or technology environment, ideally including complex, technical or scientific domains.
• Strong working knowledge of Agile/Scrum practices, with hands-on experience running backlog grooming, sprint planning and story writing.
• A track record of translating complex technical or scientific requirements into a clear, actionable product backlog.
• A collaborative approach to product ownership, with experience working in partnership with engineering teams, welcoming technical input and making trade-offs together.
• Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to work confidently across engineering, science and leadership audiences.
• Strong analytical skills and comfort using data to prioritise and justify product decisions.
Nice to Have
• Experience with MES, LIMS, ERP or other operational software used in production or laboratory environments.
• Experience with lab automation, robotics, scientific informatics or other deep-tech software platforms.
• A Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO) qualification or equivalent.
• Background or strong interest in chemistry, life sciences or automation.
• Experience working in a fast-paced, scaling startup or high-growth technology environment.
• A degree in a relevant field (computer science, engineering, life sciences or similar).
What Chemify Offers
• The opportunity to shape software at the frontier of digital chemistry.
• A collaborative, mission-driven team solving problems that don't have existing playbooks.
• Competitive salary and benefits, aligned to experience [to be confirmed by hiring manager].
• Hybrid working from Chemify's Glasgow headquarters, with up to 3 days per week in the office.
